name: Nose strip highlight

card.summary: A straight line of concealer or white highlighter down the bridge of the nose, used in gyaru makeup to make the nose look straighter and slimmer.

quick.overview:
The nose strip is a gyaru makeup technique: a narrow vertical line of concealer or white shade is drawn along the bridge of the nose. The bright line draws the eye down the centre of the face.

The visible payoff is a nose that reads as straighter and slimmer in photos and in person. It is documented as part of gyaru makeup rather than studied in research.
quick.how: Makeup users draw the line with concealer or a pale shade and blend its edges, usually alongside gyaru eye makeup such as lower-lash shadow and circle lenses. Cosmetics only; nothing is permanent.
quick.risks: It is a surface cosmetic, so risk is limited to ordinary skin reactions to products.

lead: The nose strip is one of the nose-focused techniques of gyaru, a Japanese fashion subculture whose name derives from the English slang word gal. In it, a straight line of concealer or white shade runs down the nose to make it look straighter and slimmer.[1]

It sits alongside other gyaru makeup staples: dark lower-lash shadow, drooping liner, shimmer in the eye corners, circle contacts and false lashes.[1] A rounder "button nose" contour is described as more common in some overseas communities and not conventional gyaru.[1]

chain: Light line of concealer down the bridge
Highlight catches light and focuses the centre line
angle.text: A light line down the bridge creates the impression of a straighter, slimmer nose without any procedure. It is applied as part of a full gyaru face.

paras: Wikipedia's gyaru article lists the nose strip as a core technique and notes that blush belongs on the apples of the cheeks, not the nose.[1] Gyaru itself emerged in the 1970s as a word for energetic young women, with kogal style appearing in 1992-93 and peaking through the 1990s and early 2000s before reviving in the Reiwa era via social media.[1]
